plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray, narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant tubular flowers held on long slender stems. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is a favorite of bees and butterflies. It is widely cultivated for essential oils, culinary use, and ornamental borders.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, forming a compact, suckering shrub with prickly stems and fragrant semi-double to double blooms. It is the ancestor of many garden roses and represents the classic old rose of European gardens. Mid-June is the peak of the main flush of bloom in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (June in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was grown in medieval times for medicine, and its petals keep their fragrance even when dried.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with white petals around a bright yellow center, growing on slender stems above lobed, dark green leaves. It colonizes meadows, roadsides, and grasslands and is a staple of summer wildflower displays across temperate regions. Its cheerful blooms attract many pollinators, including hoverflies and bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized across North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Oxeye daisies are in the daisy family, and each 'flower' is actually a composite of hundreds of tiny disc florets surrounded by ray florets.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: A woody Australian shrub or small tree with fine needle-like leaves and tall, cylindrical flower spikes made up of thousands of tiny flowers. It flowers in the Southern Hemisphere winter, providing vital nectar for honeyeaters, possums, and insects when other food sources are scarce. It grows in sandy, nutrient-poor soils of coastal heathland.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter in the Southern Hemisphere (April to August)
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones, often called 'banksia men' in Australian folklore, are woody and many species need fire to release their seeds.
